messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: ELB target-group unhealthy spike in us-west-2b detected for service= inference-edge. Error rate -> 502/504 rising. Spike start: 2365432098. Pager: @alice

alice (oncall-sre): on it. paging in. starting triage. ringing pagerduty. can someone confirm impact zones?

derek (oncall-app): seeing 502s from ALB logs. upstream connection resets to targets in us-west-2b. p95 request latency jumped from 120ms -> 3.2s.

caroline (prod-platform): grafana shows target health flapping only in us-west-2b AZ. other AZs healthy. ELB health check failures show TCP resets + ELB backend connection refused.

bob (network-eng): also seeing increased Route53 resolver latency for us-west-2b endpoints. dig +trace shows intermittently taking different egress path. suspect cross-AZ egress asymmetry / TGW route propagation lag.

alice (oncall-sre): ok. immediate mitigation plan:
1) shift traffic away from us-west-2b using Route53 weighted records -> increase weight for us-west-2a/2c.
2) lower Route53 TTLs to 30s for faster propagation.
3) adjust ELB healthcheck timeout -> extend to 10s temporarily.
4) scale up targets in other AZs.

eva (support): raising customer notice: "We are investigating increased 5xx errors for inference endpoints in us-west-2; working on mitigation." Will post status page update once we confirm traffic shift.

caroline (prod-platform): doing traffic shift now. running CLI to change weights.

caroline (prod-platform): ```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345XYZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2a","Weight":40,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZLWKT03EID...","DNSName":"elb-usw2a.example.amazonaws.com","EvaluateTargetHealth":true}} , {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2b","Weight":10,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZLWKT03EID...","DNSName":"elb-usw2b.example.amazonaws.com","EvaluateTargetHealth":true}} , {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2c","Weight":50,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZLWKT03EID...","DNSName":"elb-usw2c.example.amazonaws.com","EvaluateTargetHealth":true}}]}'
```

bob (network-eng): also lowering TTL on prod zone to 30s via console. pushing change-request.

derek (oncall-app): also temporarily increasing ELB healthcheck timeout and healthy threshold to avoid flapping: ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --health-check-timeout-seconds 10 --health-check-interval-seconds 15 --healthy-threshold-count 3``` 

alice (oncall-sre): scaling targets in other AZs and enabling warm pool.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: ACTION: Route53 change submitted (change id C123456789). TTL lowering and weight changes in progress.

bob (network-eng): monitoring; Route53 change applied in ~35s, but saw some caches still directing 20% to 2b for ~2 minutes. overall error rate dropped by 70% after shift.

derek (oncall-app): verifying app logs: 502s gone, 504s reduced. healthchecks stabilizing. sample curl to internal target:

```bash
curl -vv "http://10.2.3.45:8080/health" -I
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
> Content-Type: application/json
```

eva (support): posting status page update now. message: "Mitigation in progress: traffic shifted away from affected AZ; customers may experience intermittent errors while we complete failover."

alice (oncall-sre): hypothesis: a combination of (a) transient ENI detach/reattach churn in us-west-2b, (b) TGW route propagation lag causing asymmetric egress, and (c) gp3 EBS burst IO being exhausted on some targets causing p95 latency -> ELB healthcheck timeouts. Need to validate with AWS support.

caroline (prod-platform): opening AWS support case. file id: 9876543210. attaching ENI detach logs and ELB backend logs.

bob (network-eng): AWS replied: "We've seen an internal route propagation delay affecting a subset of AZ B endpoints; working on fix." They recommended draining affected ENIs and force reattach.

liz (infra): performing controlled drain of targets in us-west-2b and reattaching ENIs now. `aws ec2 detach-network-interface --network-interface-id eni-0abc123` then reattach.

alice (oncall-sre): handoff in 10m to liz (infra) for post-mitigation verification, I'm going to step off for brief rotation break. summary for handoff:
- incident start: 2365432098
- mitigation: route53 weight shift, TTL 30s, ELB healthcheck timeout extended, drained/recreated ENIs in 2b
- customer impact: ~25% requests in us-west-2 saw 5xx; overall error rate peaked at 18% account-wide for 6m
- AWS case 9876543210 opened

liz (infra): ack. will monitor until stable 1h and then restore original weights slowly.

eva (support): ticket update: customers with active sessions may have seen short failures; recommend support teams to mark impacted customers and offer 1-day credits if SLA breached. tracking ticket numbers: INC-34021.

alice (oncall-sre): marking timeline and initial blameless notes. postmortem owner: caroline. next steps: run load test on restored config, add automated runbook for route53 weighted failover, consider lowering default healthcheck sensitivity, and add probes that exercise EBS IO under load to detect gp3 credit exhaustion.

incident-bot: :tada: RESOLVED: All targets healthy and error rate back to baseline. last observed spike cleared at 2365432380. Incident status set to mitigated. Please add postmortem notes in the incident doc.

caroline (prod-platform): creating postmortem doc and assigning action items. ETA for draft: 24h.

liz (infra): leaving final note: we will keep weights at 2a/2c boosted for 15m before gradual restore to avoid oscillation. Monitoring for 1h.
